items.stem: Let X₁, X₂, …, Xₙ be a random sample from Poisson(λ), with X̄ = (1/n)ΣXᵢ and S² = (1/(n−1))Σ(Xᵢ − X̄)². Consider the statements: A. X̄ is unbiased for λ. B. S² is unbiased for λ. C. 3/10X̄ + 7/10S² is unbiased for λ. D. X̄ + S² is unbiased for λ. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: For a Poisson distribution the mean and the variance are both λ, so E(X̄) = λ and E(S²) = λ. A linear combination uX̄ + vS² then has expectation (u + v)λ, so it is unbiased exactly when u + v = 1 (negative weights are allowed). Here C has u + v = 1 and D has u + v = 2, so the true statements are A, B, C. Trap: a sum like X̄ + S² has expectation 2λ, not λ.
